sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Polyresin Vacuum Casting and Hand-Painted Limited Edition Statues

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: federal common law and federal statute; Quebec provincial private law is civil law (Civil Code of Quebec); enterprise registration and legal publicity are governed by Quebec statutes
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended by Protocols)
Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement and associated double taxation arrangement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended, with FINTRAC regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.31; Special Economic Measures Act, RSC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, RSC 1985, c U-2; Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, SC 2011, c 31; Income Tax Act, RSC 1985, c 1 (5th Supp), s 253 (non-resident carrying on business in Canada). Provincial (Quebec): Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Civil Code of Quebec, arts 2186-2237 (partnership and societe en commandite); Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11, as amended by LQ 2022, c 14; Taxation Act, CQLR c I-3; Business Corporations Act (Quebec), CQLR c S-31.1 (significant-control registers for corporate general partners). The Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) is the provincial enterprise and information gateway. No standalone public UBO register exists for limited partnerships; general partners are identified in the public REQ file, while deep UBO chain data is accessible to FINTRAC, CRA, Revenu Quebec, and police under statutory information-gathering powers.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Attestation de conformite of the corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) or Corporations Canada
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (competent authority: Ministère de la Justice du Quebec for provincial documents; Global Affairs Canada for federal documents)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and register of directors/officers of the general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or registered agent of the general partner, notarized

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport and proof of residential address for each general partner, UBO, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Quebec civil-law notary or commissioner for oaths
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization; apostille required only if the certificate will be used outside Canada

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified French translation of foreign certificate of incorporation and partnership/operating agreements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: OTTIAQ-certified translator (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interpretes agrees du Quebec)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille; translator certification only, required for REQ submission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank/PSP KYC and UBO declaration package (source of funds, business plan, payment-rail confirmation)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Institutional AML/KYC compliance officer of the banking partner, Stripe, and PayPal

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Legal opinion on Quebec limited partnership validity and limited-liability shield for non-resident limited partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille; notarial seal optional at recipient's request

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory documented screening of all partners, UBOs (25% or more), directors of corporate general partners, signatories, and third-party intermediaries against: (1) consolidated Canadian sanctions lists maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, published through the Global Affairs Canada Canadian Sanctions Database; (2) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (3) OFAC SDN List, given USD exposure through Stripe and PayPal banking partners; (4) EU and UK HM Treasury consolidated lists where applicable; and (5) domestic and foreign politically exposed persons (PEP) determinations aligned with PCMLTFA s 9.2 and FINTRAC guidance. Screening must be refreshed at formation, upon admission of any new partner, and at least annually. The proprietary Low_Risk_Standard tier permits simplified ongoing monitoring, but does not waive UBO identification, source-of-funds verification for preorder deposits, or suspicious-transaction-reporting obligations under the PCMLTFA.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) - Registre des entreprises online filing and name-analysis portal at registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, every registered enterprise name must have a French version, and that French version is the operative name analyzed by the REQ for distinctiveness and confusion. An English or other-language version may be added, but the French version prevails. Proper names, registered trademarks, and internationally recognized abbreviations may be retained in their original Latin-alphabet form; transliteration into French phonetic spelling is otherwise required. The declaration must set out the exact legal designation 'societe en commandite' or an accepted abbreviation such as 'S.E.C.' or 'L.P.' for a limited partnership; terms implying a corporate entity are prohibited.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fiducie, trust company, compagnie de fiducie
Avocat, barreau, notaire, comptable professionnel agree, ingenieur and other regulated professional titles
Royal, Reine, Gouvernement, Municipal, Police, Surete, Defense and other tokens implying public authority
Croix-Rouge, Red Cross, United Nations, ONU
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: On refusal, the REQ issues a reasoned written notice. The applicant may (i) submit a revised name proposal through the online portal; (ii) file a formal administrative review request (demande de revision) with the Registraire within 30 days of the refusal, attaching evidence of prior use, trademark registrations, or partner consents; and (iii) apply to the Court of Quebec for judicial review under the Code of Civil Procedure if the Registraire confirms the refusal. Deadlines are strict and filing fees are not refunded upon refusal or amendment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual or service-provider address is permissible as the administrative registered address for REQ purposes only where the societe en commandite maintains a genuine operational establishment in Quebec for the resin-statue production and inventory activity (e.g., a workshop or garage studio). Exclusive reliance on a virtual office without any physical Quebec presence, inventory, equipment, or operational activity would undermine tax substance under the Taxation Act and the Income Tax Act s 253, risk reassessment by Revenu Quebec, and may be treated as non-compliance with the legal publicity requirements of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate. Estimated 5-10% annualized probability of unannounced municipal zoning or by-law inspection where residential garage production is involved; approximately 3-5% for REQ or Revenu Quebec compliance visits and GST/QST audit selection; less than 2% for federal RCMP or FINTRAC on-site supervision given the Low_Risk_Standard tier designation. Maintaining municipal business permits, insurance, and clear estate signage materially reduces inspection triggers.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec, Book 8, arts. 2236-2240 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 6 and 10 (registration and disclosure obligations)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Registration Statement of a Limited Partnership)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital is prescribed by law for a Quebec limited partnership. Contributions are fixed in the partnership agreement and may be in cash or in kind. No escrow account, share premium account, or notarized capital deposit is required for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the undersigned founding general partner and initial limited partner of [Partnership Name], acting under the Civil Code of Quebec and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, hereby: 1. Ratify the subscription of the initial limited partner to the partnership interests as specified in the partnership agreement. 2. Adopt the partnership agreement dated [Date], annexed as Schedule A. 3. Appoint [General Partner Name] as the general partner vested with authority to bind the limited partnership. 4. Establish the partnership’s head office at [Address], Province of Quebec. 5. Authorize the filing of the registration declaration and all necessary annexes with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec. 6. Designate [Name] as registration agent and custodian of the partnership register. This resolution takes effect on [Date].

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - online name search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct an online name verification through the REQ portal or a recognized legal name search provider. Ensure the proposed name contains a legal element indicating limited partnership, such as 'Société en commandite', 'S.E.C.', or 'Limited Partnership'. Submit a name reservation request with two alternatives and await a written authorization of the selected name.
required_dossiers: Name search request with two proposed names
General partner name and domestic address
Agent or representative contact details if the general partner is non-resident
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised declaration of modifications or submit a new name request. A formal refusal may be challenged by written submissions to REQ within 30 days under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Partnership Agreement and Internal Governance Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner and limited partners under the Civil Code of Quebec
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft, review, and execute the partnership agreement setting out capital contributions, profit allocation, management authority of the general partner, restrictions on limited partners, dissolution triggers, and the head office clause. Each limited partner must be identified by legal name and domicile. Signatures should be dated and witnessed to evidence corporate form.
required_dossiers: Statement of contributions and capital accounts
Domicile and proof of identity for each partner
Head office address lease or consent of the owner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any factual discrepancies, re-execute the agreement, and retain a notarized affidavit of signature if REQ queries the authenticity or authority of signatories.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of Registration Statement with REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) - Online Registraire Services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite through the REQ secure portal. Indicate the partnership name, head office address, activities, general partner details, and all necessary annexes. Pay the applicable registration fee electronically. After review, REQ will issue a certificate of registration and assign the NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec).
required_dossiers: Identity and address of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If REQ issues a request for complementary information, respond within the prescribed period with the missing documents. A rejection can be administratively reviewed through a formal rectification application to the Registraire.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with Revenu Québec and CRA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ obtained from REQ, register online with Revenu Québec for QST and, if applicable, GST/HST. Open a payroll account if employees are expected and import/export accounts under the Partnership Business Number if cross-border transactions are anticipated. Confirm that the selected principal business activity maps to NAICS 339930.
required_dossiers: GST/HST registration form or online account activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Tax registration may be completed automatically through the NEQ data exchange; if conflicting account profiles arise, contact Revenu Québec’s Registre des entreprises section and submit a harmonized correction request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Partnership Register and Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General partner, acting as corporate record keeper
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create a partnership minute book containing the partnership agreement, the initial partnership resolution, a register of limited partners and contributions, and a copy of the REQ certificate. Maintain the book at the registered head office in Quebec and ensure onward updates whenever partners or addresses change.
required_dossiers: Register of limited partners and contributions
Copy of the REQ registration certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If omissions or inconsistencies are discovered, make rectification entries in the minute book and, where the public register is affected, file an application to correct the REQ record.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) - Direction de l’autorisation des projets industriels
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificat d’autorisation préalable pour exploitation industrielle (prior industrial operation authorization) under the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l’Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - declaration / registration regime for low–scale polyresin casting facilities. A full environmental impact assessment report is not required unless the facility emits more than 50 tonnes of volatile organic compounds per year or is located in a protected area designated by the provincial government.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater effluent: pH 6.0–9.5; total suspended solids ≤ 15 mg/L; oil and grease ≤ 10 mg/L. Ventilation and fugitive VOC controls must maintain outdoor air concentrations below the limits prescribed by the Regulation respecting atmospheric quality, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 4.1. Hazardous solvents (acetone, isopropyl alcohol, and resin monomers) must be stored in approved sealed containers and disposed of through a licensed hazardous waste carrier under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 32.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain a municipal fire safety clearance under the Quebec Fire Safety Act, CQLR c. F-2.1, proving compliance with fire-resistance walls, solvent storage cabinets, extinguisher coverage, and evacuation routes. Secure a structural load inspection and occupancy certificate from the local municipality verifying the floor can support casting machinery and storage racks. Register with CNESST under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c. S-2.1, implement a written prevention program, and provide WHMIS training for workers handling resin, catalysts, and solvents.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax; Revenu Québec for Quebec QST and provincial income tax. Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html) and Revenu Québec CléSec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca/).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a non-resident-owned Limited Partnership: 1) Submit Form RC1 to CRA to obtain a Business Number (BN) for the partnership, including GST/HST account (unless small supplier and elects not to register). 2) Register for QST with Revenu Québec via the Partnership Registration form (if taxable sales in Quebec exceed $30,000 CAD). 3) File T5013 Partnership Information Return annually for income allocation; each partner files separate T1/T2 reporting their share of income. 4) Non-resident partners without SIN require a CRA Individual Tax Number (ITN) via Form T1261. 5) For electronic services, consider CBCA/CRNRA compliance; nexus depends on place of supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent for both federal and Quebec income tax; partners bear tax on allocated income. However, for GST/HST and QST, the LP is treated as a separate 'person' and must register and file separately if it makes taxable supplies and is not a small supplier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box election. Tax transparency is mandatory. Available elections: (i) partnership non-calendar-year-end election under ITA s. 249.1; (ii) GST/HST and QST input tax credit allocation elections under ETA s. 141.1 and QST Act s. 401 if the partnership has multiple businesses or related members.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax) – federal; QST (Quebec Sales Tax) – provincial
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD of worldwide taxable supplies (GST/HST) and $30,000 CAD of taxable supplies in Quebec (QST) over any current or four consecutive calendar quarters; zero-rated exports count as taxable supplies for threshold determination.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate currently applies. CRA and Revenu Québec accept electronic invoices if the supplier guarantees integrity, authenticity, and readability. Quebec has announced a phased e-invoicing mandate (B2B) targeted to begin around 2027, but it is not in force. No statutory API or pre-clearance approval is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to sales of goods delivered to a non-resident purchaser outside Canada, provided the goods are exported directly and leave Canada within 60 days. GST/HST Schedule VI Part V Section 1 and QST Act Schedule IV Section 1. Services (e.g., custom resin casting) performed for non-residents are zero-rated if not linked to real property or tangible personal property in Canada. Proof of export (customs declaration, transport documentation) and evidence of payment from the buyer are required. No statutory FX repatriation deadline; a 180-day documentary consistency rule is commonly applied by auditors for export corroboration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A or CBSA Electronic Export Report)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Proof of Consideration in foreign currency (bank transfer, Stripe/PayPal payout record)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec can reassess within four years (extended to 10 years for misrepresentation). Gross negligence penalties under ETA s. 285.1 and QST Act s. 170 are up to 25% of the net tax evaded plus interest. False statements may attract a separate penalty of 25% of the tax attributable to the false statement. Criminal fraud charges under ETA s. 327 and QST Act s. 175.1 expose the perpetrator to fines up to $500,000 and imprisonment up to five years. Export zero-rating will be reversed retroactively if documentation is incomplete, with full GST/QST, arrears interest, and penalties clawed back.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); exchange-rate and foreign-exchange reserve policy is vested in the Minister of Finance under the Currency Act, with the Bank of Canada acting as fiscal agent. Prudential regulation of Schedule I and II deposit-taking institutions is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) under the Bank Act (Canada). In Quebec, the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) supervises financial-markets conduct, payment-service-provider registration, and derivatives, but does not regulate chartered-bank treasury operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. Canada has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations; no exchange-control approvals apply to profit remittance, distributions to non-resident limited partners, or repatriation of capital. A Quebec société en commandite may invoice export sales in USD or any currency and hold the proceeds in a foreign-currency account at a Canadian bank without conversion mandate. Legal constraints are limited to: (i) FINTRAC reporting of international wire transfers and large transactions of C$10,000 or more; (ii) cross-border currency declarations of C$10,000 or more; and (iii) Investment Canada Act notification if a non-resident limited partner acquires control of a Canadian business. No Exchange Control Act regime exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory deadline, no mandatory surrender percentage, and no conversion ratio for export proceeds. The Quebec LP may accumulate USD receivables indefinitely and convert at its chosen commercial timing, subject only to the functional-currency consistency rules of the Income Tax Act and the Taxation Act (Quebec). Mandatory administrative duties are: (a) FINTRAC large-transaction reports for each receipt of C$10,000 or more and for every verified international wire transfer of C$10,000 or more; (b) customer identification and record keeping under the PCMLTFA; and (c) retention of the underlying commercial invoices, bills of lading, and customs declarations to evidence the trade origin of the funds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Laurentian Bank of Canada (Banque Laurentienne du Canada)
Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium, with defined legal constraints. Stripe Payments Canada, Ltd. and PayPal Canada Co. are FINTRAC-registered payment service providers and the preferred settlement rails for card-based preorders; they must settle in CAD to the LP's Schedule I operational account. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Payoneer) are not Canadian licensed banks, are not CDIC-insured, and cannot hold client funds in a segregated deposit account protected under Canadian banking law. They may operate only as money-services businesses (MSBs) registered with FINTRAC or as foreign-entity conduits for FX conversion and small-value payouts. An offshore EMI cannot support a 'Capital Escrow Account' with enforceable Canadian segregation, and reliance on an EMI as the primary clearing bank creates FINTRAC reporting ambiguity and weakens the audit trail required by Revenu Québec. Recommended posture: use a Schedule I bank as the primary treasury and clearing tier; deploy EMIs only as secondary conversion and disbursement utilities.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires physical presence for a domestically registered Quebec LP. If the general partner is a Canadian resident, National Bank, BMO, and RBC accept remote video identification under their PCMLTFA-compliant procedures. If any limited partner is non-resident, or the general partner is a non-resident entity, banks will require a Canadian-resident signatory to attend an in-person or enhanced video interview, with notarized passports, proof of address, the REQ registration extract, the partnership declaration (contrat de société), a general-partner resolution authorizing account opening, and specimen signatures. Beneficial-ownership disclosure must identify every partner holding at least 25% of the partnership interests and the natural persons behind any corporate partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Preorder deposits received via Stripe and PayPal prior to product delivery, flagged by transaction monitoring as possible layering, consumer-deposit-taking, or unexplained customer prepayments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (a) PSP merchant settlement statements mapping every preorder to customer email, order ID, and card digit; (b) the standard preorder terms of sale with refund policy; (c) the LP's public website and catalogue evidencing resin statue production; (d) fulfilment invoices issued at shipment; (e) a business-model narrative by the general partner; and (f) operational expense records demonstrating the deposits fund production rather than financial intermediation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner capital contribution routed from a jurisdiction with weak AML enforcement, creating an unexplained source-of-wealth gap.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (a) signed partnership agreement and capital-account ledger; (b) a bank reference from the contributor's home institution; (c) six months of source-of-funds statements (salary, dividends, or disposition documents); (d) a sworn source-of-funds affidavit; (e) corporate registry extract and beneficial-ownership chart if the contributor is an entity; and (f) sanctions screening confirmation covering GAC, OFAC, and UN lists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large export disbursements to resin suppliers in higher-risk or sanctioned-adjacent jurisdictions, flagged for possible diversion, sanctions evasion, or export-control breach.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (a) supplier contract and purchase orders; (b) supplier KYC file with business registration and beneficial-owner declaration; (c) end-user and end-use attestation for the resin material; (d) ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930 trade classification with HS codes; (e) shipping documents (B/L or AWB) and customs declarations; and (f) completed sanctions screening matrix for all named counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid conversion of USD export receipts to CAD with immediate onward disbursement, flagged as potential structuring or trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (a) export sales forecast and production cash-flow model; (b) USD account statements tracing invoice-to-settlement-to-conversion; (c) FX spot or forward confirmations; (d) supplier payables schedule; and (e) a written treasury note confirming conversion timing is driven solely by supplier payment due dates and the LP's functional-currency election.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Execute a capital contribution agreement and general-partner resolution prior to the wire. Instruct the non-resident investor to send a SWIFT MT103 to the receiving Schedule I bank in CAD, quoting the LP's legal name as registered with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and a purpose code of 'Capital contribution - limited partner'. National Bank of Canada: SWIFT BIC BNDCCAMMINT; BMO: BOFMCAM2. Remittance-reference fields are limited by SWIFT standards and must contain only the investor reference; no supplementary narrative is permitted. The account must be funded as a non-operating capital inflow, and the LP should file the relevant financing statement or rely on the Quebec accredited-investor exemption in the partnership capital structure. Capital contributions are exempt from exchange-control approval. Preorder deposits via Stripe and PayPal will settle through the PSP's Canadian acquiring entity into the operational account net of pre-agreed fees; the association 'E-commerce sale of resin statues (ISIC 3240)' must be preserved as settlement descriptor for audit integrity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic supplier payments under C$25,000: Interac e-Transfer or ACSS EFT credit. Domestic amounts of C$25,000 or more requiring same-day finality: LVTS wire transfer. US suppliers: SWIFT MT103 via Fedwire/CHIPS correspondent, or the bank's US-dollar clearing hub (e.g., BMO New York branch) for ACH and USD cheques. Asian resin suppliers: irrevocable Documentary Commercial Letter of Credit issued under UCP600 at sight or 30/60-day usance, collateralized at 100% of the L/C value plus margin by the bank, with documents comprising commercial invoice, packing list, and B/L or AWB. Preorder refunds: reverse chargeback through the original Stripe/PayPal rail. All outgoing international wire transfers of C$10,000 or more trigger FINTRAC reporting; the LP must retain the underlying transaction log and commercial documentation for at least five years.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable CAD/USD and CAD/EUR FX forwards (maturities up to 24 months) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex, with unsecured or margin facilities extended to the LP

Non-deliverable FX forwards (NDFs) referencing non-convertible Asian currencies (CNY, INR, IDR) with CAD settlement at the WM/Reuters or ECB fix, permissible for hedging forecast resin import payables
Cross-currency swaps and FX swaps converting USD preorder receivables into CAD at matched tenors, eliminating translation risk in the LP's capital accounts

Zero-cost collars and plain-vanilla FX options layered on the forward programme, transacted as OTC derivatives under the Quebec Derivatives Act and reportable to the AMF only if the LP exceeds the end-user exemption thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec Annual Declaration (Déclaration annuelle) — corporate existence and partnership registry return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — Quebec Enterprise Registrar
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 6th month following the LP's fiscal year-end (e.g., June 15 for a December 31 fiscal year-end); no statutory extension is available for partnerships.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: supplementary administrative late fee payable to the REQ; failure to file for two consecutive fiscal years triggers a formal Registrar notice and administrative strike-off of the LP from the Register of Enterprises. Offence fines: CAD 200–2,000 (individuals) or CAD 500–5,000 (partnerships) under the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return (Summary and T5013 slips) — annual allocation of partnership income and losses to partners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 5 months after fiscal period end (e.g., May 31 for a December 31 fiscal year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under Income Tax Act s. 162(7.2): CAD 25 per day per partner, minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500 per partnership; willful false statements trigger civil penalties up to CAD 25,000 and criminal prosecution under s. 239.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: TP-600 Partnership Information Return — Quebec annual partnership declaration and partner allocation schedule
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 6 months after fiscal period end (e.g., June 30 for a December 31 fiscal year-end).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty: CAD 25 per day per partner (minimum CAD 100, maximum CAD 2,500); gross negligence penalty of 50% of misreported amounts; continued default permits Revenu Québec to assess estimated partnership income and pursue judicial collection.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No blanket statutory audit is imposed on Quebec limited partnerships. An independent audit becomes compulsory when: (a) the LP is a reporting issuer or publicly distributes securities under the Quebec Securities Act; (b) the LP is an investment fund or alternative fund subject to NI 81-106; (c) the partnership agreement, a lender, or a regulator requires audited statements; or (d) CRA or Revenu Québec formally demands audited financial statements. Practical market trigger: gross revenue exceeding CAD 2,000,000 and/or total assets exceeding CAD 1,000,000, at which institutional counterparties and lenders routinely require audited statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Publicly accountable LPs: IFRS as published in the CPA Canada Handbook. Private LPs: Canadian ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) or a no-public-accountability IFRS election; tax basis and the partnership fiscal period must be reconciled consistently with the Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Taxation Act (Québec).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Since March 31, 2023, the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises requires every Quebec LP to disclose control persons and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) in the REQ declaration. The LP must identify any individual holding 25% or more of the partnership interests (measured by capital or profit share) or exercising direct or indirect de jure or de facto control. The annual declaration requires an attestation that UBO data remains current; any transfer of a partnership interest that changes control or crosses the 25% threshold must be declared to the REQ within 15 days of the transfer, not merely at the annual filing. The annual register audit compares the on-site Register of Partners, the minute book, and transfer ledgers against the REQ declaration and the T5013/TP-600 partner allocation schedules.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (Register of Members) — full name, domicile, capital contributions, profit-loss shares, and transfer dates for all general and limited partners
Register of General Partner and Managers — appointments, removals, mandates, and management resolutions (partnership equivalent of a register of directors)
Minute Book — convening notices, annual meeting minutes, resolutions, capital calls, and distribution approvals

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 250–800 per year (CAD 350–1,100) for a standard Quebec registered office and registered agent; fully managed packages including annual declaration preparation, UBO register upkeep, and minute book filing typically range USD 500–1,200.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–12,000 (CAD 4,200–16,500) per annum for a small-to-mid-sized polyresin statue manufacturer; a review engagement costs USD 1,500–3,500, while a full ASPE/IFRS audit with inventory valuation, revenue recognition, and inter-partner allocation procedures sits at the higher end.
